i18n.datasets.api.filter.af_learned_or_p: Occupations to be included to survey occupations learnt
i18n.datasets.api.filter.description.af_: This filter (ACTIVE) enables current or archived occupational titles to be selected. The archived titles are kept for historic purposes and allow data to be retropolated for the revision of a classification but may no longer be used for current surveys.
Occupation titles used in public employment services

Certain occupation titles are only useful to survey the occupations learnt. This is especially the case for academic diplomas. We recommend adding these titles for questions concerning the occupation learnt (LEARNED OR PRACTICED).
i18n.datasets.api.filter.description.afc: The duplicate filter (DUPLICATE) enables duplicate titles to be deleted. Occasionally, two titles (or more) are translated by a single title in another language (DUPLICATE). Rather than needlessly repeating the same title, the corresponding fields are left empty to avoid superfluities when displaying suggestions during surveys or when coding occupations by entering the letters in full.

The “Selection of occupational titles” (REDUCED LIST) can be used to integrate occupational titles into surveys conducted via internet or telephone or for other online forms. This list is a sub-set of the list of occupations available to the FSO. It contains the most commonly mentioned occupations, avoids superfluities or occupations that are problematic or too vague, as well as a sometimes too detailed description of occupations in the list (level of detail not required for codification in the classification). Occasionally, two titles (or more) are translated by a single title in another language. Rather than needlessly repeating the same title, the corresponding fields are left empty to avoid superfluities when displaying suggestions during surveys.
i18n.datasets.api.filter.info: Some filters should not be used in combination. The «Selection PLASTA» filter should not be used in combination with other filters, the «Selection for surveys» filter only with the carried out and/or learnt occupation.

i18n.distribution.mediatype.popover.desc: A media type, also known as a MIME type, describes the type of content of a medium. It consists of a main type and a subtype. These are separated by a slash. Examples: a table in CSV format is described with "text/csv", a web page in HTML with "text/html". The specification of the media type is used to determine how content is to be interpreted and processed. Such specifications are used by the web browser or e-mail program, for example.
